newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close down, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close down, seen falling.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed down as shortage ended on higher supplies from ginning factories and are likely to fall on Thursday when the market reopens after Wednesday's holiday, dealers said.
The NIAB-78 variety closed 27.50 rupees lower at 2,645.50 per maund (37.32 kg) and the MNH-93 27.50 at 2,690.
In the kerb market, the rate for the NIAB-78 closed at 2,275 rupees per maund, plus 10 percent sales tax, one dealer said.
The rates are likely to fall in the next few days owing to higher picking at farms, the dealer said.
The private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said exports had reached 1.82 million 375-lb bales by August 25 since the 1995/96 picking season began on September 1, 1995.
